themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis THIS WEEK
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 129 this week—537% above the 8-week average of 20.2 per week—marking the most severe week-to-week spike in district infrastructure complaints, with a z-score of 10.8 indicating a genuine emergency-level deviation.
evidence: 129 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 20.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (537% spike)
Z-score of 10.8 indicates statistically extreme deviation (severity: high)
266 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (217 alterations) suggest active construction that may be damaging streets
reporting_angles: Are active construction projects (217 alterations in 90 days) tearing up Forest Hills and Rego Park streets faster than DOT can repair them?
Interview DOT district manager and construction inspectors about root causes of this week's spike and repair timeline

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Forest Hills
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints exploded to 6 this week—1500% above the 8-week baseline of 0.4 per week—signaling either a new tagging campaign or deteriorating neighborhood conditions that warrant immediate cleanup and investigation.
evidence: 6 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike)
Z-score of 8.08 indicates statistically extreme and genuine outbreak
Concentrated spike suggests organized tagging or single crew activity rather than gradual deterioration
reporting_angles: Is there a new tagging crew active in Forest Hills? Photo-document locations and patterns.
Contact NYPD Graffiti Task Force and Parks Department about coordinated response

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Spreading
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal complaints jumped to 70 last week—239% above the 8-week average of 20.6 per week—creating potential safety hazards across Forest Hills' busy intersections and suggesting systemic electrical or maintenance failures.
evidence: 70 traffic signal complaints last week vs. 20.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (239% spike)
Z-score of 5.16 indicates high statistical significance
Yellowstone Boulevard, 108-05 68th Road, and Queens Boulevard are active rezoning sites where infrastructure upgrades may be planned or underway
reporting_angles: Which intersections are affected? Map complaints and conduct safety audit at busiest ones.
Interview DOT about whether infrastructure work for ongoing ULURP rezonings has disrupted signal timing or maintenance

themes_detail.label: School Maintenance Emergency
themes_detail.summary: School maintenance complaints spiked to 8 three weeks ago—1500% above the 8-week average of 0.5 per week—indicating urgent facility or heating issues affecting student learning conditions in district schools.
evidence: 8 school maintenance complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike)
Z-score of 15.0 is the highest statistical deviation in dataset
Heat/hot water remains largest category overall (2,098 complaints over 90 days), suggesting winter facility crisis may still be ongoing
reporting_angles: Which schools filed complaints? Were heating systems failing during cold weather in early January?
Interview parents and DOE about whether students missed school days due to unsafe conditions

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints increased to 9 this week—350% above the 8-week average of 2.0 per week—suggesting widespread building or infrastructure decay across the district's residential and public facilities.
evidence: 9 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (350% spike)
Community Board budget requests include 'renovate or upgrade senior center' and 'expand parks/amenities'—suggesting long-deferred maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: What facilities are failing? Survey apartment buildings, senior centers, Parks Department properties for deferred maintenance.
Connect spike to CB budget history: what maintenance requests have gone unfunded year after year?
